speaker: A
text: Hello, come in and take a seat. Thanks for coming along today. Before we start, I just want to remind you that this is a practice session, and we have about ten minutes together.

speaker: B
text: Okay, thank you. That sounds fine.

speaker: A
text: So, what would you like to talk about today?

speaker: B
text: Well, I have been feeling quite overwhelmed with the house move. There is so much to organise, and I keep putting things off until the last minute.

speaker: A
text: Mm-hm.

speaker: B
text: Then I end up doing everything late at night, and I am exhausted the next day at work.

speaker: A
text: It sounds like the move is taking up a lot of your energy, and the more tired you get, the harder it is to make a start.

speaker: B
text: Yes, exactly. That is exactly it. I look at the list and I just freeze.

speaker: A
text: You freeze. What is that like for you, in the moment?

speaker: B
text: It is a bit like standing at the bottom of a very big hill. I know I have to climb it, but I cannot see where the path begins.

speaker: A
text: That is a very clear picture. A big hill, and no obvious first step.

speaker: B
text: Right.

speaker: A
text: I wonder what the smallest possible first step might look like?

speaker: B
text: Probably just packing one box. The books in the spare room, maybe. That would take twenty minutes.

speaker: A
text: One box of books. How does it feel when you say that out loud?

speaker: B
text: Honestly, a bit lighter. It sounds silly, but one box feels possible.

speaker: A
text: It does not sound silly at all. You noticed that when the task is smaller, the feeling changes.

speaker: B
text: Yes. I think I have been looking at the whole hill, and not at my own feet.

speaker: A
text: Okay. We are coming towards the end of our time. Is there anything you would like to take away from today?

speaker: B
text: I will pack one box tonight, and I will stop looking at the whole list. Thank you, this has really helped.

speaker: A
text: You are very welcome. Thank you for sharing that with me.
